lead.t: Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a rare, congenital bone marrow failure syndrome that usually becomes symptomatic in early infancy.

snip.t: Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a rare, congenital bone marrow failure syndrome that usually becomes symptomatic in early infancy.

qs.q: What is the typical age of presentation for Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA)?
o: More than 90% of cases are recognized in the first year of life
Most cases become symptomatic only after five years of age
It almost exclusively presents during the adolescent years
Symptoms reliably appear exclusively in the third year of life
qs.e: Diamond-Blackfan anemia is a rare congenital bone marrow failure syndrome where more than 90% of cases are recognized in the first year of life. Adolescence is well beyond the typical early infancy presentation window.

qs.q: Which genetic mechanism is most commonly identified in Diamond-Blackfan anemia?
o: Mutations in ribosomal protein genes with autosomal dominant inheritance
X-linked recessive mutations affecting platelet surface glycoproteins
Mitochondrial DNA deletions inherited exclusively from the maternal line
Trisomy of chromosome 21 leading to ineffective erythropoiesis
qs.e: Since the majority of causative mutations in DBA are in RP genes, the disorder is often referred to as a ribosomopathy, with most following an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern. X-linked recessive glycoprotein mutations are typically associated with bleeding disorders rather than DBA.

qs.q: What laboratory finding helps distinguish Diamond-Blackfan anemia from transient erythroblastopenia of childhood (TEC)?
o: Increased erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity in red cells
Normal serum iron levels without any bone marrow changes present
Marked elevation of fetal hemoglobin levels in all clinical phases
Presence of hypersegmented neutrophils on the peripheral smear
qs.e: Erythrocyte adenosine deaminase (eADA) activity is increased in most patients with DBA, a finding that helps distinguish it from acquired TEC where eADA levels are normal. TEC does not feature megaloblastic changes like hypersegmented neutrophils.

qs.q: What is a primary mainstay of therapy for Diamond-Blackfan anemia when treating the bone marrow failure?
o: Corticosteroids such as prednisone or prednisolone administration
High-dose intravenous immunoglobulin monotherapy treatment course
Immediate hematopoietic stem cell transplantation at birth
Serial therapeutic phlebotomies to reduce iron overload states
qs.e: Corticosteroids are a mainstay of therapy for DBA, with 80% of patients initially responding to agents like prednisone at 2 mg/kg/day. IVIG is used for persistent parvovirus infections in immunodeficient patients, not as the primary therapy for DBA.

qs.q: Why is Diamond-Blackfan anemia considered a cancer predisposition syndrome?
o: Patients have a higher risk of myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, and solid tumors
Chemotherapy agents used in infancy permanently alter cellular DNA repair mechanisms in bone marrow
Repeated blood transfusions directly induce malignant transformation of circulating lymphocytes
Chronic corticosteroid exposure inevitably leads to malignant hepatic cell carcinomas over time
qs.e: DBA is a cancer predisposition syndrome because affected individuals carry a higher risk of developing myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, colon carcinoma, osteogenic sarcoma, and female genital cancers. Transfusion-related iron overload causes endocrine abnormalities, not the primary cancer predisposition.

qs.q: How do laboratory parameters in transient erythroblastopenia of childhood (TEC) generally compare to Diamond-Blackfan anemia?
o: Red blood cell adenosine deaminase levels are normal in transient erythroblastopenia of childhood, unlike elevated levels in Diamond-Blackfan anemia
Mean corpuscular volume is significantly elevated in transient erythroblastopenia of childhood with marked macrocytosis throughout
Platelet counts are consistently severely depressed in transient erythroblastopenia compared to normal counts in Diamond-Blackfan
Fetal hemoglobin levels are markedly elevated throughout the active phase of transient erythroblastopenia of childhood
qs.e: RBC adenosine deaminase levels are normal in TEC, thus contrasting with the elevation noted in most cases of congenital hypoplastic anemia. The MCV in TEC is typically normal for age, unlike the macrocytosis seen in DBA.

qs.q: What is the typical age of presentation for more than 90% of patients with Diamond-Blackfan anemia?
o: In the first year of life
Between 6 and 10 years
During early adolescence
After 12 years of age
qs.e: Diamond-Blackfan anemia is a rare congenital bone marrow failure syndrome that usually becomes symptomatic in early infancy, with over 90% of cases recognized within the first year of life. Adolescence is incorrect as the vast majority present much earlier.

qs.q: Which of the following laboratory findings specifically helps distinguish Diamond-Blackfan anemia from transient erythroblastopenia of childhood?
o: Normal platelet count levels
Increased erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity
Presence of marked reticulocytopenia
Decreased bone marrow cellularity percentage
qs.e: Erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity is increased in most patients with Diamond-Blackfan anemia, which helps distinguish it from acquired transient erythroblastopenia of childhood where levels are normal. Reticulocytopenia occurs in both conditions, making it unhelpful for differentiation.
